CommonLifecycleModel.description:
Lifecycle phases for common models.

Maps phase names to phase configurations. Phase names follow the pattern ``{command}_{action}_{suffix}``, e.g. ``deploy_plan_before``, ``deploy_provision``, ``deploy_destroy_after``, ``config_clear``. This is an open map (any phase name is allowed) rather than a fixed set of fields, since each kind and provisioner type defines its own set of supported phases.

CommonLifecyclePhaseModel.description: Lifecycle phase configuration: a description plus its scripts.

scripts.description: Scripts to run. Each entry is a path relative to the solution root, with one of the extensions bash, go, js, mjs, ps1, py, sh, or an object with `file`, `scope`, `priority` and `target`.

DeploymentAssetBindingModel.description: Rebind one workspace asset slot to another Asset for this deployment, for example a customer's own API definitions. The bound document is used as it is, never patched. There is no bare-string shorthand.

asset.description: Asset document bound to the slot for this deployment

DeploymentDocumentationModel.description:
Render the handover document at the end of every successful `deploy run` and store it with the audit record: the same document `strata deploy report --format markdown` renders, with the run's own audit entry. Secret values are never in it; secrets are listed by where to find them.

Rules:
- Needs the workspace's `output_store`: the document is built from what it recorded.
- `sink: audit` needs an enabled `git` audit sink in the Configuration: only a git sink stores files.
- `template` must exist and may only use the report's data (`deployment`, `workspace`, `environments`, `steps`, `secrets`, `images`, `audit`, `generated_at`, `MASK`).

template.description: A Jinja2 template, relative to the solution root, that replaces the built-in Markdown. It receives the same data as `strata deploy report --output json`; no field in it holds a secret value.

sink.description: Where the document goes. `audit`: written as `_handover.md` next to the audit manifest and pushed with it by every enabled `git` audit sink.

DeploymentHealthCheckModel.description:
A reachability probe to run after a stage: an `http` check needs `url`, a `tcp` check needs `host` and `port`. Accepted and validated, but strata does not use it yet.

Rules:
- An `http` check needs `url`; a `tcp` check needs `host` and `port`.

name.description: Unique health check name within the stage

DeploymentLayersModel.description:
Position of this deployment in a hierarchy. `follows` names a path convention from the Configuration's `spec.paths`, and `segments` gives the values for that convention's segments.

Strata compares `segments` with the values captured from the directory the document lives in: an unknown `follows` is an error, and a disagreeing value is a warning or an error depending on the convention's `enforcement`. The segments also shape the audit output path. They are never filled in from the directory when absent.

follows.description: Name of the path convention this deployment's hierarchy follows

segments.description: Resolved values for that convention's segments (e.g. {'control': 'dev'})

DeploymentLockingModel.description: Pipeline-level state locking, to stop concurrent runs from colliding. Accepted and validated, but strata does not use it yet.

strategy.description: 'wrap' makes strata take its own lock around the whole run; 'delegate' leaves locking to the provisioner's own state backend (e.g. Terraform's).

wait_timeout.description: How long to wait for a held lock before failing (e.g. '10m')

force_unlock_after.description: Age after which a stale lock may be broken (e.g. '1h')

params.description: Parameter sets this deployment reads, per role: `{spoke: spoke-acme-001}`, or a list per role merged in order (`{hub: [hub-defaults, hub-hub02]}`). Any document of the extends chain may name sets: per role they merge root first, leaf last, later winning per leaf key, so a base's sets are defaults and the leaf's override them. `${param:<role>.<key>}` in the spec of any document of the chain reads the merged values. Not inherited as meta: each document names its own.

name_rule.description: The name every deployable deployment built on this one must have, with `${param:<role>.<key>}` tokens filled from that deployment's parameter sets (`bootstrap-${param:spoke.name}`). A deployment whose meta.name differs is a `name_rule_mismatch` error that gives both names: names stay plain text, but cannot drift from their values. Only `${param:}` tokens are allowed.

tags.description: Optional tags (list of values for categorization)

DeploymentProviderBindingModel.description: Rebind one workspace provider slot to another Provider for this deployment, for example the same workspace deployed to a second Azure region. The bound document is used as it is, never patched. There is no bare-string shorthand, because a binding only matters when it differs from the workspace's default.

provider.description: Provider document bound to the slot for this deployment

DeploymentSpecModel.description:
What to deploy, where and how: the `workspace` whose recipe runs, the `environments` supplying values, an optional `tenant` and `version` pins, provider and asset rebinding, and per-step runtime `stages`. `partial` and `extends` share a base between deployments.

Rules:
- A step may have `stages` parameters declared only once.
- An environment may be listed only once, and a provider slot or asset slot may be bound only once.
- `kube_context` and `docker_context` are context names as written; a value token is rejected.
- A deployable document needs `workspace` and at least one entry in `environments`. A `partial: true` document, or one with `extends`, is exempt because its missing fields come from the base.

partial.description: When true this is a reusable base that is not deployed on its own: required fields may be absent and it is not checked against the rest of the solution. Another deployment uses it through `extends`.

extends.description: Name of a base Deployment document whose spec is merged into this one before validation. Child always wins: nested blocks deep-merge per leaf key, `stages` merge by `step`, `environments` append after the base's, other lists are replaced. Circular chains are rejected. Distinct from `environments` layering, which composes *values*; this composes *structure*.

workspace.description: Name of the Workspace document whose provisioning recipe this deployment runs

environments.description: Names of Environment documents supplying values, merged in order — later entries win. A tenant's own `environments` merge in before these.

tenant.description: Name of the Tenant this deployment belongs to. Omit for shared/platform deployments that serve all tenants.

kube_context.description: Name of the context in the caller's kubeconfig that this deployment's Helm steps deploy to. When set, every `helm` call runs against this context, whichever context is active, and the deploy stops before the first `helm` call when the kubeconfig has no such context. The caller still provides the kubeconfig. Omit to use the active context; `strata validate` then warns for a deployment with a Helm step. Value tokens are not allowed here.

docker_context.description: Name of the Docker context (`docker context create`) that this deployment's Compose steps deploy to. When set, every `docker` call runs against this context, and the deploy stops before the first step when Docker has no such context or `DOCKER_HOST` is set (it would override the context). Omit to use whatever engine the environment points at; `strata validate` then warns for a deployment with a Compose step. Value tokens are not allowed here.

configurations.description: Names of additional Configuration documents that apply to this deployment. Accepted and validated, but strata does not use it yet.

version.description: The Version document, or list of Version documents, supplying pins for this deployment. The pins of every listed document apply together; two listed documents pinning the same target is an error (`version_pin_conflict`), so a shared document (`prd-core`) and a product document (`prd-datahub`) each own their own pins. Through `extends` the lists append, base first. When a pinned target (image, chart, remote ref, artifact tag, asset ref) is declared elsewhere, the pin wins. Omit to use each document's own declared versions.

layers.description: Hierarchy position: a path convention to follow and the segment values for it.

documentation.description:
Render the handover document (step outputs, secrets by location, images) at the end of each successful `deploy run` and store it with the audit record. Off when unset.

Rules:
- Needs the workspace's `output_store`: the document is built from what it recorded.
- `sink: audit` needs an enabled `git` audit sink in the Configuration: only a git sink stores files.
- `template` must exist and may only use the report's data (`deployment`, `workspace`, `environments`, `steps`, `secrets`, `images`, `audit`, `generated_at`, `MASK`).

locking.description: Pipeline-level state locking. Accepted and validated, but strata does not use it yet.

stages.description:
Runtime parameters per workspace provisioning step

Rules:
- Health check names must be unique within the stage.

providers.description: Rebind workspace provider slots to other Provider documents for this deployment. Merged by `slot` across `extends` (child wins), so a partial base can bind a region once.

assets.description: Rebind workspace asset slots to other Asset documents for this deployment. Merged by `slot` across `extends` (child wins), so a partial base can bind some slots and a leaf others.

lifecycle.description: Hook scripts per phase name. Accepted and validated, but strata does not run lifecycle hooks yet.

properties.description: Deployment properties, the last merge layer over the tenant's and the environments' properties, passed to Terraform as `strata.properties`. Add an `attributeconfig` with `target.kind: deployment` to validate them.

custom.description: Free-form values merged over the tenant's and the environments' `custom` values (the deployment wins), passed to Terraform as `strata.custom`. Strata does not interpret them.

DeploymentStageModel.description:
Runtime parameters for one provisioning step of the workspace, named by `step`. A stage never redefines what runs. Today strata applies only `timeouts`; the other fields are accepted and validated but not used yet.

Rules:
- Health check names must be unique within the stage.

step.description: Name of the workspace `execution` step these parameters apply to.

enabled.description: Intended to switch the stage on or off. Accepted and validated, but strata does not use it yet. Every step runs. A string is a conditional expression, which is not evaluated either.

on_failure.description: What a failed stage should do: `stop` (default), `rollback` or `continue`. Accepted and validated, but strata does not use it yet.

timeouts.description: Per-phase timeout overrides, applied by `deploy run`.

health_checks.description:
Reachability probes to run after this stage succeeds. Accepted and validated, but strata does not use it yet.

Rules:
- An `http` check needs `url`; a `tcp` check needs `host` and `port`.

scripts.description: Additional scripts for this stage. Accepted and validated, but strata does not use it yet.

secrets.description: Secret keys this stage needs injected from the Environment. Accepted and validated, but strata does not use it yet.

namespace.description: Restrict this stage to a single namespace. Accepted and validated, but strata does not use it yet.

helm_namespaces.description: Restrict a Helm or sync stage to these namespaces. Accepted and validated, but strata does not use it yet. A Helm step deploys every namespace of its step.

DeploymentStageTimeoutsModel.description: Per-phase timeouts in seconds that override a provisioner's defaults. The environment variable `STRATA_TIMEOUT_<STEP>_<PHASE>` overrides them for a single run.

ScriptPathModel.description: Individual script with scope and execution metadata.

scope.description: Execution scope - determines how many times the script runs (e.g. deployment, environment, workspace, provider, resource, module, namespace)

priority.description: Execution order within scope (lower runs first)

ScriptsModel.description: Model for validating script paths with scope-aware execution.

scripts.description: Scripts to run. Each entry is a path relative to the solution root, with one of the extensions bash, go, js, mjs, ps1, py, sh, or an object with `file`, `scope`, `priority` and `target`.

ParamToken.description: Filled from the document's parameter sets when the solution loads (`${param:<role>.<key>}`).

description:
A deployment of a workspace: runs the workspace's recipe with the values of its environments, for an optional tenant and pinned version. Create one per place a workspace is deployed, such as a customer, a ring or a region, and share structure through a `partial: true` base and `extends`.

Rules:
- A deployment cannot extend itself; longer extends cycles are rejected when the chain is resolved.

spec.description:
Deployment specification (workspace, environments, stages)

Rules:
- A step may have `stages` parameters declared only once.
- An environment may be listed only once, and a provider slot or asset slot may be bound only once.
- `kube_context` and `docker_context` are context names as written; a value token is rejected.
- A deployable document needs `workspace` and at least one entry in `environments`. A `partial: true` document, or one with `extends`, is exempt because its missing fields come from the base.
